title: Diagnosis result: ways to fix it (fix_options)
description: How to fill result_summary.fix_options. A diagnosis should lead with how to fix it. The options are alternatives a person picks from, not a to-do list. A client sends them only when server_capabilities lists fix_options_v1 and the client advertised fix_options_v1 at pickup. A client that did not advertise it has its options removed with a warning. Tellagen never runs a fix, never writes to a code host and never posts to a vendor: the client proposes and a person decides. The client never sends a label, an address or an action type; Tellagen works out what each button does from the kind of the option and its one target.

x-handlers.create_action: Creates an action item on the incident. Label: Create action.
x-handlers.vendor_issue: Drafts an issue for a vendor of the reviewed catalog. Label: Draft the <vendor> issue. A vendor that is not in the catalog gets: Copy the issue text, and no link.
x-handlers.hand_off: Creates an action item for the team the problem belongs to. Label: Hand off to <team>…
x-handlers.assign_rollback: Creates an action item that asks a person to roll back to the last good deployment. Label: Assign rollback to…
x-handlers.close: Closes the ticket as expected behavior, after a person confirms. Label: Close as expected behavior…

x-warnings.fix_option_unread_file: A change names a file that is not in this run's trace or evidence. It cannot be recommended and is shown as not checked against your code. Read the file before you propose a change to it.
x-warnings.fix_option_without_verify: The option has no sentence that says how a person checks that it worked.
x-warnings.fix_option_diff_too_large: The change is more than 6 changed lines, or the diff is not a valid diff block. The diff is removed: name the file and the owner instead.
x-warnings.fix_option_multiple_recommended: More than one option is recommended. Only the first offered one stays.
x-warnings.needs_fix_without_option: The verdict is real_problem and no offered option is a permanent fix or a mitigation.
x-warnings.leave_as_is_with_exposure: Leave as is is recommended while the verdict is real_problem, held, or customer impact is not verified as none.
x-warnings.hand_off_without_target: A hand-off option names neither a team nor a vendor.
x-warnings.fix_option_dropped: An option was removed: over the limit, an unknown value, no title, no reason for a state that needs one, more than one target, or a target that is not valid.
x-warnings.fix_option_recommends_when_not_sure: The verdict is not_sure. A diagnosis that is not sure recommends nothing.
x-warnings.change_step_without_runbook: A step that changes a system (deploy, rollback, restart, scale, a flag, a purge) has no runbook step a person wrote behind it, so it was removed. Read-only verify commands stay.

x-errors.fix_option_invalid: 400. A client that advertised fix_options_v1 sent an unknown kind, where, state, effort or risk.

x-guidance: Lead with how to fix it. Give 2 to 5 options and recommend at most one. The recommended option is an offered one.

Read before you recommend. A change to code or configuration is recommended only if you read the file in this run. Name it in read_refs (repo, path, ref_or_sha, lines) and keep the step that read it in the trace. A file you did not read is shown as not checked against your code.
Keep the change small. A diff is for a change of at most 6 changed lines. A larger change has no diff: name the file and the owner.

A tempting wrong option stays in the list. If it would do harm, set state not_recommended and say why in state_reason. If it is harmless but does not fix this, set state no_effect. Use not_recommended only for harm.
Name at most one target: vendor {key, issue_title, issue_body}, hand_off {team_id} or rollback {change_ref_id, runbook_ref}. Never send a label, a web address or an action type.
For a vendor, use the key of the vendor. Write the issue so a stranger can follow it, with no secret and no customer data.

A rollback names a change ref of the same result with the role last_good and the kind deployment or release. You cannot know how the team rolls back. Name a runbook step only when the pickup showed one; otherwise leave runbook_ref out. Never write a deploy, rollback, restart, scale, flag or purge command yourself.
A verify command is read-only. Say in verify.text what the person should see.
When the verdict is not_sure, recommend nothing.
Leave as is closes the ticket as expected behavior. Recommend it only when the verdict is not a real problem, the case is not a held expected behavior, and customer impact is verified as none.

fix_options.title: Report the rejected test cookie to PostHog
trade_offs: Takes days to be fixed upstream
The console warning stays until then

verify.text: The warning is gone after the vendor releases a fix, or the issue is acknowledged.

vendor.issue_title: Test cookie on a public suffix is rejected by the browser
vendor.issue_body: The vnd_chk_ test cookie is set on .com, which browsers reject by design. The library should skip the check for public suffixes.

fix_options.state_reason: It would split the visitor identity between the site and the workspace subdomains.
fix_options.title: Turn off cross-subdomain cookies
trade_offs: Breaks the shared visitor identity that was set up on purpose

fix_options.title: Leave it: the browser rejects the test cookie by design

verify.text: Tracking events keep arriving in the product analytics.

bad.why: Recommends a change to a file the run never read, sends its own label and a deploy command, and has two recommended options.
